data.one_liner: A Flutter widget that lets users drag any widget freely around the screen.
data.what_it_does: Allows developers to implement a floating widget that can be dragged freely across the screen. It supports physics-based animations, automatic alignment to screen edges, and an optional widget deletion zone.
use_when: You want to implement floating action buttons or mini-players that users can drag around.
You need a widget that auto-aligns to the left or right side of the screen after dragging.
You require a deletion target zone when dragging widgets.
avoid_when: You need the widget to float over other native mobile applications outside your app.
You need automatic calculation of the parent widget's or floating widget's size.
strengths: Supports physics-based animations and auto-alignment options.
weaknesses: Does not float over other system apps.
Requires manual sizing for both parent and floating widgets.
data.minimal_example:
FloatingDraggableWidget(
  mainScreenWidget: Scaffold(
    appBar: AppBar(title: Text('Demo')),
    body: Center(child: Text('Body')),
  ),
  floatingWidget: FloatingActionButton(
    onPressed: () {},
    child: const Icon(Icons.add),
  ),
  floatingWidgetHeight: 40,
  floatingWidgetWidth: 40,
  dx: 200,
  dy: 300,
)
